reconcile.connective: Commentators read Colossians 2:18's "not seen" as false teachers' claimed private visions, distinct from the revealed, unseen realities faith embraces elsewhere.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain conflict: Hebrews 11:1 exalts faith in the unseen while Colossians 2:18 condemns it.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Should we believe in unseen things?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/unseen.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013), "Should we believe in unseen things?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: Paul, not stopping to discuss the nature of the things so seen, fixes on the radical error, the tendency of such a one in all this to walk by SENSE (namely, what he haughtily prides himself on having SEEN), rather than by FAITH in the UNSEEN "Head" (Col 2:19; compare Joh 20:29; Co2 5:7; Heb 11:1).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names the resolution: the 'not seen' Paul condemns is the false teacher's self-vaunted sensory vision (walking by SENSE), explicitly opposed to FAITH in the unseen Head — and cross-references the very three reconcile-side verses (John 20:29, 2 Cor 5:7, Heb 11:1) this row's summary cites as the 'command' pole.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The false teachers were evidently saying they had had visions that established certain rituals as requirements for the community.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Independently identifies the referent of 'not seen' as the false teachers' claimed mystical visions used to impose rituals — a distinct, modern voice reaching the same harmonizing distinction as JFB, without the visions-of-Christ or faith-in-God's-promises sense Hebrews and 2 Corinthians use.

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible, on Colossians 2:18
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: JFB's note on Colossians 2:18 (already the reconcile pole's primary excerpt) reads the false teacher's 'not seen' as vaunted sensory experience opposed to faith in the unseen Head, and cross-references John 20:29, 2 Corinthians 5:7, and Hebrews 11:1 by name — the exact cluster this row's contradiction turns on. Haley's An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874) does not appear to treat this specific pairing; a harmonizing commentator already surfaced on the row is used per spec.
